reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Chiropractic practice defined and distinguished from medicine
headings.reviewNote: Read both subsections and history. Subsection 1 defines the practice, its exclusions (surgery, obstetrics, osteopathy, podiatry, drugs) and the declaration that it is not medicine under chapter 334.

headings.title: Meridian therapy and acupuncture certification
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 says practice "may include" meridian therapy/acupressure/acupuncture with board-required certification; permissive, not mandatory.

headings.title: Board meaning in chapter
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 only construes "board" as the state board of chiropractic examiners; history cites A.L. 2023 S.B. 157.

headings.title: Animal chiropractic definitions
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 defines animal chiropractic and practitioner (licensed veterinarian, or licensed chiropractor with certification and 210 hours); includes limits on diagnosis, surgery, and medications; cross-refs 331.010 and 340.200.

headings.title: Optional fingerprint requirement for applicants
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 says the board "may" require fingerprints with a license application; cross-refs 331.010. History: L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174.

headings.title: Patrol submission when fingerprints required
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 applies only if the board requires fingerprints; background check through highway patrol, state and federal.

headings.title: Fingerprint handling and record access
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 3 covers repository search, FBI forwarding under 43.540, patrol notice to board, and board access notwithstanding 610.120.

headings.title: License required to practice chiropractic
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 prohibits practice without a license under this chapter.

headings.title: Application form and contents
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 covers sworn application contents, evidence of education, and board determination about schools.

headings.title: Education and examination eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 3 covers pre-doctoral credit hours (not fewer than ninety), CCE-status graduation, and senior-student practical exam; no license until all requirements are met.

headings.title: Fees and reexamination
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 4 covers nonrefundable fees, deposit in chiropractic board fund, and possible reexamination on board-rule conditions.

headings.title: Licensure by examination requirements
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 5 covers NBCE written parts, practical and law exams, license issuance on rule standards, and no credit for correspondence work.

headings.title: License without examination for foreign licensees
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 6 covers foreign-licensed applicants with equivalent standards, one year of practice and fee; board may require SPEC if not equivalent.

headings.title: Additional study after repeated practical failures
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 7 requires a semester of study for applicants failing a practical exam portion three times, as board rule provides.

headings.title: Meridian therapy certification
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 8 covers certification application and fee before practicing meridian therapy/acupressure/acupuncture, board rules, and the definition.

headings.title: Board-authorized specialty certifications
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 9 says the board "may" authorize specialty certifications by rule, subject to education requirements and a scope limit tied to 331.010 (subdivisions 1-2).

headings.title: License renewal and continuing education
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 covers renewal fee, postgraduate hour ranges, one-year notice of increases, waiver for illness or good cause, mailed notice, display of licenses, and no excuse for non-receipt of form.

headings.title: Lapsed license reinstatement
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 says a lapsed license "may" be reinstated on explanation and fees; more than five years out of practice requires study and practical exam.

headings.title: Inactive license status application
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 3 covers application, board determination, and limits on practice for inactive or retired licensees.

headings.title: Continuing education during inactive status
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 4 exempts inactive licensees from continuing education requirements during inactivity.

headings.title: Return to active status from inactive
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 5 covers return within five years with notice, fees, board requirements, and no licensing exam.

headings.title: Board may refuse licenses; written notice to applicant
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 says the board "may" refuse for subsection 2 causes, with written notice and advice on filing a complaint with the administrative hearing commission (chapter 621).

headings.title: Grounds on which board may file discipline complaint
headings.reviewNote: Covers the permissive 'may' complaint to the administrative hearing commission for any of 21 grounds, including advertising sub-items (a)-(f) and (21) fitness-to-practice reexamination and board orders; navigation summary only.

headings.title: Board discipline options after commission finding
headings.reviewNote: Covers chapter 621 proceedings and, after a commission finding, board options (censure/probation up to five years, suspension up to three years, revocation). The Seger v. Downey annotation (on 2(14)) is in the notes, not here.

headings.title: Absence or unlicensed time excluded from discipline period
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 4 excludes time out of state, unlicensed, or unknown whereabouts from the discipline period.

headings.title: Fee setting and board fund
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 covers fees set by rule under 536.021, cost-related limit, collection, deposit in the board fund, and expense limit.

headings.title: Fund transfer to general revenue limit
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 states the lapse threshold at two or three times the preceding appropriation, notwithstanding 33.080.

headings.title: Board application for emergency suspension or restriction
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 conditions the board's request on a pending criminal charge related to duties and reasonable cause of imminent harm. History: L. 2026 S.B. 1233; severability clause cross-reference § 1.1009.

headings.title: Complaint filing and service packet
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 covers affidavits, court records, one-business-day service packet, and 24-hour service on the licensee.

headings.title: Initial order review within five days
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 3 covers commission review, findings, entry of requested order if reasonable cause found, and effectiveness on service.

headings.title: Evidentiary hearing and continuation of order
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 4 read with subdivisions (1)-(3): 45-day hearing, 120-day outer limit, amendment, termination or continuation of order, board hearing afterward.

headings.title: Emergency action in addition to other discipline
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 5 says action is additional to other discipline and may be concurrent.

headings.title: Removing records if no initial order
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 6 requires board to remove references from public records if the commission does not grant an initial order under subsection 3.

headings.title: Injunction or restraining order applications
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 covers court orders on board application for unlicensed practice or substantial danger, subdivisions (1) and (2).

headings.title: Venue for injunction action
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 sets venue in the county of conduct or defendant's residence.

headings.title: Injunction in addition to other penalties
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 3 says action is additional to chapter penalties and may be concurrent.

headings.title: Chapter 334 licensee exception
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 4 says section does not prohibit chapter 334 licensees in good standing from acting within their scope. History: L. 1999 H.B. 343 merged with S.B. 8 & 173.

headings.title: Public member qualifications

headings.title: Seal, rules, quorum, and examination notice

headings.title: Board personnel

headings.title: Personnel duties and compensation limits

headings.title: Patient record contents and format
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 covers adequate records, electronic format, and seven listed information items with cross-references to 331.010.

headings.title: Record retention period
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 2 requires seven-year retention of records under licensee custody from last service.

headings.title: Late changes to patient records
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 3 covers marking and identifying changes made over forty-eight hours later, with date, time, name, reason.

headings.title: Discipline limits for record violations
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 4 bars discipline solely on this section; permits alleging it as an additional cause under 331.060 if other discipline begins.

headings.title: Board access to patient records
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 5 requires written patient authorization or subpoena.
